text:
Elaine: hey team — I pushed the followup for PR #9874. Addressed the comments: moved the batching config to runtime, added a migration test, tightened the kvcache locking around the allocator, and fixed the race Rajesh pointed out. PTAL when you have a minute.
Sam: thanks — skimmed, looks good overall. left one optional nit about using structured logging for the batch decisions, up to you.
Rajesh: quick question — will this change the default batch size for legacy pools? worried thin clients might see different tail-latency.
Elaine: good q. default is preserved; I added a migration test and a feature flag `enable_new_batching` (default: false) so existing deployments keep behavior. docs in the PR describe the rollout steps.
Sam: nice. also can you include the short command we ran for the integration smoke? would help ops replicate.
Elaine: added snippet in the PR description:
```
./tools/run_integration.sh --pool=dedicated --batch-size=auto --smoke --metrics=debug
```
CI Bot: CI passed: linux-integration build 4523 ✅ (windows flake retried).
Sam: :thumbsup: I can merge once you decide on squash vs keep history. any preference?
Elaine: squashed and pushed as a single commit `batching: runtime-config + migration test`. CI green.
Rajesh: canary target? we should limit initial canary to dedicated pools in us-west only.
Elaine: set canary to `dedicated` + region `us-west-2`, window 2h. will watch latency dashboards and set rollback alert.
Sam: SGTM. PTAL final time and merge if nothing pops up in canary.
Elaine: thanks! tagging @Sam and @Rajesh again for final eyes :)
